s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of skin and muscle symptoms following immunotherapy
salient_findings: Muscle weakness and limited joint mobility
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Has stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma
Metastases in liver, lungs, and peritoneum
Developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab treatment
Received a second course of ipilimumab 14 months later
Experienced recurrence and worsening of symptoms
Physical findings include photodistributed erythematous eruption and diffuse erythema
Elevated creatine kinase levels (1088 U/L and 1854 U/L)
Aldolase level is 23.0 U/L
C-reactive protein level is 28.6 mg/L
Antinuclear antibody titer is 1:640 with speckled pattern
Jo-1 antibody is negative
MRI shows mild short TI inversion recovery hyperintensity of bilateral vastus lateralis and rectus femoris muscles
Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy shows atrophy of type II muscle fibers

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has photodistributed erythematous eruption, elevated creatine kinase levels, and atrophy of type II muscle fibers, consistent with dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Ipilimumab-induced myositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed skin and muscle symptoms after starting ipilimumab treatment, suggesting an association with the immunotherapy

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has stage IV malignant melanoma and developed dermatomyositis-like symptoms, raising the possibility of a paraneoplastic syndrome

shortlist.label: Necrotizing autoimmune myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated creatine kinase levels and muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers, which could be consistent with necrotizing autoimmune myopathy

shortlist.label: Checkpoint inhibitor-induced dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed dermatomyositis-like symptoms after receiving ipilimumab, a checkpoint inhibitor, suggesting a possible association

raw.rationale: The patient developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab treatment, a checkpoint inhibitor, and experienced recurrence and worsening of symptoms after a second course, which is consistent with checkpoint inhibitor-induced dermatomyositis. The patient's physical findings, such as photodistributed erythematous eruption and diffuse erythema, and laboratory results, including elevated creatine kinase levels and antinuclear antibody titer, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms are consistent with dermatomyositis, the temporal relationship with ipilimumab treatment suggests a checkpoint inhibitor-induced condition.

rejected.label: Ipilimumab-induced myositis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are more consistent with dermatomyositis than myositis alone.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While the patient has malignant melanoma, the temporal relationship with ipilimumab treatment suggests a checkpoint inhibitor-induced condition rather than a paraneoplastic syndrome.

rejected.label: Necrotizing autoimmune myopathy
rejected.why: The patient's muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers without evidence of inflammatory myositis or necrosis, which is not consistent with necrotizing autoimmune myopathy.
